slice: v2 tape files [4000:4300] (mid-tape), 42.4M maker fills, 24.8M trade-price points
method: per MAKER fill, forward price = first taker trade in [t+DELTA, t+DELTA+max(2*DELTA,900)]; markout_ps = (side=BUY? p_fwd-p_fill : p_fill-p_fwd); negative = adverse selection
verdict: Overall maker markout POSITIVE at every horizon 60s..1day (dollar-wtd +0.0021..+0.0056/share) -> makers are NOT systematically adversely selected; they capture the spread.
Spearman(maker volume, markout) ~= 0 at all horizons (+0.004..-0.027) -> the v1 -0.58 (maker PnL vs counterparty EVENTUAL win-rate) is the outcome/zero-sum identity, NOT fill-time picking-off.
Only negative cell in the grid: smallest-maker decile at 60s (-0.0026); reverts to +0.011 by 300s. Adverse selection is a sub-minute, small-maker-only, transient effect.

Small makers earn HIGHER per-share markout than large (d1 +0.011..+0.028 vs d10 +0.003..+0.006) beyond 60s -> opposite of 'amateurs absorb AS'. Dollars concentrate in high-volume makers (volume, not per-unit edge).
Maker edge = SPREAD CAPTURE (positive markout), not adverse-selection avoidance.
caveats: v2 (fee era) execution markout vs v1 (archive) realized PnL - complementary, not merged; a maker can have +markout and still lose realized PnL (inventory/holding to resolution/fee).
Coverage falls with horizon (83% at 60s -> 11% at 1day): longer-horizon and illiquid-token makers under-covered; speaks to liquid-market making.
